text: Now Naomi had a relative on her husband's side, a man of standing from the family of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz.
Ruth the Moabite said to Naomi, Let me go to the fields and gather the leftover grain behind anyone who will allow it. Naomi said to her, Go ahead, my daughter.
So Ruth went out and began to glean in the fields behind the harvesters, and as it happened, she came to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was from the family of Elimelech.
Just then Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and greeted the harvesters, The LORD be with you! They answered, The LORD bless you!
Boaz asked the young man in charge of the harvesters, Whose young woman is this?
The young man answered, She is the young Moabite woman who came back with Naomi from the country of Moab.
She asked if she could glean and gather among the sheaves behind the harvesters. She came out and has remained here from morning until now, except for a short rest.
Then Boaz said to Ruth, Listen, my daughter. Do not go to glean in another field, and do not leave here, but stay close to my young women.
Watch which field the men are harvesting, and follow behind them. I have told the young men not to touch you. And whenever you are thirsty, go and drink from the water jars they have filled.
Ruth fell to the ground and bowed low, saying, Why have I found such favor in your eyes, that you would notice me, a foreigner?
Boaz replied, I have been told everything you have done for your mother-in-law since your husband died — how you left your father, mother, and homeland to come to a people you did not know before.
May the LORD repay you for what you have done, and may you receive a full reward from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.
Ruth said, I hope I may continue to find favor in your eyes, my lord. You have comforted me and spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not even like one of your servants.

At mealtime Boaz told her, Come here and eat some bread, and dip your piece in the wine vinegar. So she sat beside the harvesters, and he handed her roasted grain; she ate all she wanted and had some left over.
When she got up to glean again, Boaz ordered his young men, Let her gather grain even among the standing sheaves, and do not embarrass her.
In fact, pull out some stalks from the bundles on purpose and leave them for her to gather, and do not rebuke her.
So Ruth gleaned in the field until evening, then threshed what she had gathered, and it came to about an ephah of barley.
She carried it back to town, and her mother-in-law saw how much she had gathered. Ruth also brought out what she had left over from the meal and gave it to Naomi.

Naomi asked her, Where did you glean today? Where did you work? Blessed be the man who noticed you. So Ruth told her mother-in-law whose field she had worked in, saying, The name of the man I worked with today is Boaz.
Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, Blessed be he by the LORD, who has not stopped showing kindness to the living and the dead. That man is a close relative of ours, one of our redeemers.
Ruth the Moabite added, He even told me, Stay close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.
Naomi said to Ruth, It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that in someone else's field you might not be harmed.
So Ruth stayed close to the young women of Boaz to glean until the barley and wheat harvests were finished, and she continued living with her mother-in-law.
